subject.title: Support multiple gateway tokens for multi-user session isolation

question: Should OpenClaw add native multi-token Gateway principals for token mode, or should multi-user isolation remain delegated to trusted-proxy/front-layer designs such as Pinchy?
rationale: This is not a narrow bug fix: it introduces new credential semantics, per-token identity, scope decisions, and session attribution in a security-sensitive Gateway surface.

options.title: Sponsor native token principals
options.body: Define a first-class token principal model with labels, scopes, rotation/audit behavior, and session identity, then implement it as a coordinated Gateway auth design.

options.title: Defer to identity-bearing front layers
options.body: Keep token/password mode as a single operator secret and document trusted-proxy or front-layer patterns as the supported multi-user path.

options.title: Split the identity work
options.body: Handle per-message author attribution and scope-bound service tokens in the linked narrower issues before deciding whether per-user token mode should exist.

recommendation.title: Sponsor native token principals
recommendation.body: Define a first-class token principal model with labels, scopes, rotation/audit behavior, and session identity, then implement it as a coordinated Gateway auth design.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Gateway auth guard and trusted-proxy history plus issue subscription make this the best available routing candidate from the inspected history.
